o.text: From sarı (“yellow”) + -şın, which is otherwise only attested in qaraşın and in the borrowed name Aqşın.
Borrowed from Classical Persian سُمَّاق (summāq), from Arabic سُمَّاق (summāq).

From qızıl + -ca.
Cognates
Cognate with
Bashkir ҡыҙылса (qıðılsa)
Kazakh қызылша (qızılša, “measles”),
Kyrgyz кызылча (kızılca, “measles”),
Kumyk кызылча (kızılça, “rubella”),
Uzbek qizilcha (“rubella”).

Inherited from Proto-Common Turkic *bognuk (“stifling;”) from *bog- (“to strangle”). Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (boğnaqlān-, “to get cloudy”), Chagatai [script needed] (boğnak, “rainless storm; muffled noise; stifling”), Salar boğunaq (“thunder”), Turkish boğanak (“heavy rain”), boğunuk (“muffled noise”).
